utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: He was a -- an army officer, a JNA army officer. I believe that he was retired. But sometime in early April or in May, he was working in the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did he later become the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, which was based in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he was the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, if you mean Nedeljko Anicic. I am not sure that he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did he have something to do with the 6th Krajina Brigade? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: He did. In the preparation -- I believe that he was the main person in the staff of the 6th Krajina Brigade and that he was also in the Crisis Staff. I think he was involved in making plans -- in the planning, that is, together with the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade. He was the most important military person in the command staff of the 6th Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the commander was the most important person, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander is the most important person, but Anicic, Mr. Nedjeljko Anicic, was in the staff. He was the Chief of Staff of the Serbian defence, of the Serb defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And just let's deal with that for the moment. During the events that we are going to deal with in 1992, who was the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, when the aggression started on the municipality of Sanski Most in 1992, was Lieutenant Colonel or Colonel of the former JNA, Branko Basara.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to move, then, to the events after the war in Croatia started. Once the war in Croatia started in June of 1991, was the 6th Krajina Brigade -- or rather, was mobilisation ordered?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: After the 6th Krajina Brigade was returned to Sanski Most from the front in Croatia, from the Republic of Croatia, mobilisation followed in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I think we may be -- it's my fault. The war started in June of 1991. Did the 6th Krajina Brigade go straight to Croatia before mobilisation was ordered?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise answer. I cannot recall. I cannot remember the dates. But I know, and I do remember, that the 6th Krajina Brigade, the Sanska Brigade, as part of the JNA, took part on the front in the Republic of Croatia during the war. I know this because many reservists of the 6th Krajina Brigade were released from having to do their work, their place of employment, because they were mobilised, and they went to the front.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, I interrupted. Was there something else you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC
utterances.text: While they were at the front, they were receiving a salary at their place of employment in the company, and I also know that the members of the 6th Krajina Brigade and the reservists who were Bosniak or Croat, they did not want to go to the front in Croatia, except for some exceptions. They deserted. When there were shifts of parts of the 6th Krajina Brigade returned to Sanski Most, very often there was a disturbance of security among the population, and this created tensions in a certain way among the population of Sanski Most because people came from the front with weapons that they then carried through the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, that may be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner, and I thank you, Judge. We will continue tomorrow. There is one very small matter that I wanted to raise. You filed a motion to redact part of the transcript relating to Witness BT12 because there was a moment when we should have been in private session and we weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you had time, Mr. Ackerman and Maitre de Roux, to go through that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I have no objection, Your Honour.
